b: (Æ)Lab:999 is a new open-access, peer-reviewed forum for work in philosophical aesthetics. All submissions to it must be no more than 999 words long.
The executive editor of the journal is Aaron Meskin (University of Georgia). Its managing editor is Danielle Kotrla and its assistant managing editor is Alex Hollatz-Guastella.

The journal’s editorial consultants are Rok Benčin, Adriana Clavel-Vazquez, Ley David Elliette Cray, John Dyck, Brandon Polite, Jon Robson, Brooke Rudow, Elizabeth Scarbrough, Karen Simecek, Roland Végső, Jonathan Weinberg, Mary Beth Willard, and Rissa Willis.

We are especially interested in works that aim to explore a historically-underrepresented or underexplored topic in philosophical aesthetics or the philosophy of art. Submissions should therefore be fully academic—such that they possess the features of traditional academic writing and are for an academic audience.

Some possible topics of interest might include, but are in no way limited to: reality television, vernacular dance, amateur aesthetics, dog shows, fanfiction, fashion, cocktails, romance novels, clowns, contact improvisation, artistic collaboration, puppets, AI slop, interior design, bluegrass, poetry readings, slang, and typefaces. We welcome contributions that engage with these topics, others, and more traditional topics through philosophical argumentation and analysis. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive philosophical dialogue, and welcome submissions from members of underrepresented and marginalized groups.
You can learn more about (Æ)Lab:999 here.
